study_material.title: Time and Work - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: If A finishes a job in x days, A does 1/x of it per day. Add daily rates to combine workers, invert to get days. Every time-and-work puzzle - joint work, leaving mid-way, wages, efficiency - reduces to rate arithmetic.
learning_objectives: Handle workers joining or leaving mid-job
Split wages in proportion to work done
Use man-days for group problems and efficiency scaling

concepts.heading: 1. Rates Add
concepts.body: A in x days means rate 1/x per day. A and B together: rate = 1/x + 1/y, days = xy/(x+y). Three or more workers: keep adding rates. To find one worker from a pair: subtract rates, e.g. B = (A+B rate) - (A rate).

concepts.heading: 2. LCM Method
concepts.body: Take the LCM of the given day-counts as total work units. If A does 12-day work and B 24-day work, set work = 24 units: A does 2/day, B does 1/day, together 3/day - finish in 8 days. Integer units avoid fraction errors.

concepts.heading: 3. Partial Work and Departures
concepts.body: Compute work done in the joint phase, subtract from 1 (or from total units), then divide the remainder by the remaining workers' rate. For alternate-day problems, compute one full cycle's work and count cycles.

concepts.heading: 4. Efficiency
concepts.body: 'A is twice as good as B' means A's rate is double, so A's time is half. If A is k times as efficient, times are in ratio 1:k (inverted). A 20% more efficient worker needs time/1.2.

concepts.heading: 5. Wages
concepts.body: Wages are shared in proportion to work done, i.e. in proportion to rates when time worked is equal. A doing 1/6 per day and B doing 1/9 per day share wages 3:2 (invert the day counts and simplify).

formulas: Work left = 1 - (joint rate x joint days)
Efficiency k times means time divided by k
Wages ratio = rate ratio (for equal duration)
shortcut_methods: Use LCM units instead of fractions
For pairs given as A+B, B+C, C+A: sum all three to get 2(A+B+C)
Alternate-day problems: work per 2-day cycle first
common_mistakes: Forgetting to subtract the completed fraction before the second phase
Mapping 'twice as efficient' to twice the time instead of half
study_material.summary: Work with per-day rates (or LCM units), add them for teamwork, subtract for departures, and invert at the end for days.
quick_revision_notes: 2(A+B+C) = sum of the three pair rates

solved_examples.step_by_step: Let A take x days, B takes 2x. 1/x + 1/2x = 3/2x = 1/12, so x = 18.
solved_examples.shortcut: A does 2 of every 3 units; total time x = 12 x 3/2.

questions.question: 4 men and 6 women finish a job in 8 days; 3 men and 7 women finish it in 10 days. One woman alone would take:
questions.explanation: 8(4m+6w) = 10(3m+7w) gives 32m+48w = 30m+70w, so 2m = 22w, m = 11w. Total work = 8(44w+6w) = 400 woman-days.
